title: Finite-etale weak-solution transfer with perfect lower residue field
statement: Let $U\to D\to V$ be injective local maps of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq F\subseteq M$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $D$ is finite etale over $U$: finite as a $U$-module, with $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}U$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume the residue field $U/\mathfrak m_U$ is perfect (every algebraic extension is separable; equivalently, in positive characteristic $p$, Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective). Assume $V$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. For an injective local map $X\to Y$ of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $P\subseteq Q$, call a finite field extension $H/P$ a weak solution if, writing $R_H$ for the integral closure of $X$ in $H$ and $C_H$ for that of $Y$ in $(Q\otimes_PH)_{\mathrm{red}}$, every maximal ideal $q$ of $C_H$ has maximal contraction $n=q\cap R_H$, both $(R_H)_n$ and $(C_H)_q$ are DVRs, and $n(C_H)_q=q(C_H)_q$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Reduction is quotient by all nilpotents, finite field extension means finite-dimensional, and local means pulling back the maximal ideal. If some finite field extension $H/F$ is a weak solution for $D\to V$, then there exists a finite field extension $N/K$ which is a weak solution for $U\to V$. No completeness assumption or perfectness assumption on the residue field of $V$ is made. The conclusion is existence of $N$; it does not assert that the given field $H$, merely regarded as a $K$-extension, is a weak solution.

source.place: Tag 09ET (lemma-solution-after-strict-henselization), final finite-etale coefficient step, corrected to perfect lower residue. Tag 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), transitive normal-extension action on normalized upper branches; Tags 09EN (definition-solution), 0GLR (lemma-solution-goes-up), and lemma-extension-dvrs-formally-smooth in this document; see proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, first proof sentence, for weak solution = solution over perfect lower residue. Agent normal-compositum repair of the faulty 09ET conjugate-factor assertion, detailed in report.md.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree], $F/K$ is finite. Products of finite field bases show that $H/K$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension] choose $H\subseteq N$ finite normal over $K$; in particular $N/H$ is finite. Write $R=\operatorname{IntCl}_D(H)$ and $S=\operatorname{IntCl}_D(N)$. The ring $D$ is integral over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Consequently $R=\operatorname{IntCl}_U(H)$ and $S=\operatorname{IntCl}_U(N)$: an element integral over $U$ is integral over $D$ by the same monic equation, and the reverse implication is [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent]. Thus the chosen normal extension will have exactly the lower normalization required in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09ET, final coefficient step; normal enlargement replaces the conjugate-factor assertion; normal closure: fields.tex Tag 09DT

proof.text: Put $C_H=\operatorname{IntCl}_V((M\otimes_FH)_{\mathrm{red}})$ and choose a maximal ideal $q$ of $C_H$. Such ideals exist by the nonempty dimension-one product assertion of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure]. Set $n=q\cap R$, $A=R_n$, $B=(C_H)_q$. The hypothesis that $H/F$ is a weak solution gives $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$. The same structure node gives $A,B$ DVRs and $\kappa(n)/\kappa(D)$ finite. Also $\kappa(D)/\kappa(U)$ is finite: the quotient $D/\mathfrak m_D$ is a quotient of the finite $\kappa(U)$-vector space $D/\mathfrak m_UD$. Hence $\kappa(n)$ is algebraic over the perfect field $\kappa(U)$ and is perfect by [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect]. Every finitely generated subextension of $\kappa(B)/\kappa(A)$ is separably generated by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis]. This is exactly separability of the possibly transcendental extension in [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 09EN, weak-solution hypothesis; Tag 09EM, finite residue extensions; Tag 09II, first proof sentence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] to $A\to B$ and $N/H$, using the fraction field $H$ of $A$. Every resulting local normalized branch has lower maximal ideal generating its upper maximal ideal. By [lem-sfb-normalized-finite-coefficient-tower] applied to $D\to V$ and $F\subseteq H\subseteq N$, these are precisely the local branches of $C_D=\operatorname{IntCl}_V((M\otimes_FN)_{\mathrm{red}})$ over $q$, with lower ring $S_m$ at the corresponding contraction $m$. At least one such branch exists by the lying-over clause of that node. Fix it, say $Q_D$; then $m(C_D)_{Q_D}=Q_D(C_D)_{Q_D}$. This uses the residue separability established in Step 2, so does not assume stability of arbitrary weak solutions.

source.place: Tag 0GLR, solution permanence, implemented branchwise by Tag 09EM local normalizations

proof.text:
Finite etale base change [lem-fet-finite-limits] makes $T=V\otimes_UD$ finite etale over $V$. Its residue algebra is a finite product of finite separable residue extensions by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. As $V$ is strictly henselian, these fields are all $\kappa(V)$. The equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] therefore lifts that decomposition to $T\cong\prod_{j\in J}V$. The given inclusion $D\to V$ defines the retraction $T\to V$, $v\otimes d\mapsto vd$, which selects one coordinate: the coordinate idempotents map to $0$ or $1$ in the domain $V$, exactly one maps to $1$, and its $V$-algebra map $V\to V$ is the identity. Inverting a uniformizer of $U$ gives $M\otimes_KF\cong\prod_JM$, with potentially DIFFERENT $F$-structures on the factors; the selected factor has the given $F\subseteq M$. Tensoring over $F$ with $N$ and reducing gives
$(M\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\prod_{j\in J}(M_j\otimes_FN)_{\mathrm{red}}$,
where each $M_j=M$ as an $M$-algebra but carries its own $F$-structure. The selected factor is $(M\otimes_FN)_{\mathrm{red}}$; no equality of the other factors is asserted. These tensor identifications follow on pure tensors from [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Integral closure over $V$ respects this finite product: a tuple of integral elements is killed by the product of their monic equations, and projection preserves integrality. Thus $C_D$ is a direct factor of $C=\operatorname{IntCl}_V((M\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}})$. The branch $Q_D$ gives a maximal ideal $Q_0$ of $C$ with $C_{Q_0}=(C_D)_{Q_D}$, and its contraction in $S$ is the same $m$. Step 3 gives $mC_{Q_0}=Q_0C_{Q_0}$.

source.place: Tag 09ET, third proof paragraph, finite etale splitting over the strict upper DVR; keep the distinct coefficient embeddings instead of identifying conjugate tensor factors

proof.text: For any maximal ideal $Q$ of $C$, apply [lem-sfb-normal-coefficient-branch-conjugacy] to $U\to V$ and $N/K$. Choose $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(N)$ carrying $Q_0$ to $Q$. It carries $m=Q_0\cap S$ to $n=Q\cap S$, and the local isomorphism $C_{Q_0}\to C_Q$ carries $mC_{Q_0}$ to $nC_Q$ and $Q_0C_{Q_0}$ to $QC_Q$. The equality from Step 4 therefore becomes $nC_Q=QC_Q$. Finally [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], now for $U\to V$ and $N/K$, gives maximal contraction and both DVR assertions at every $Q$. Thus this finite $N/K$ satisfies every clause of the weak-solution definition in the item.
